title: Sen. Lindsey Graham dies, leaving Senate seat vacant
summary: The longtime South Carolina Republican chaired the Senate Budget Committee and led a key appropriations panel.

title: Trump empties out election commission leadership just months before midterms
summary: Career staff can continue day-to-day operations, but the leadership gap could affect decisions on voting technology, standards and federal election programs.

title: Fired EPA dissenters sue for reinstatement, alleging First Amendment violations
summary: Seven former EPA employees said they were targeted for removal for signing an open “declaration of dissent” in their personal capacities because they had fewer civil service protections rather than any wrongdoing.

title: IRS missed hiring goals for 2026 tax season, which watchdog says impacted service performance
summary: The tax agency temporarily reassigned hundreds of employees to cover the gaps in staffing.

title: Calls grow for an independent probe into fatal Houston ICE shooting
summary: House Democrats are demanding body camera footage and answers from DHS and ICE, arguing the agencies have yet to back up their public account of the encounter.

title: Transportation loses its top tech official amid wave of CIO departures
summary: Pavan Pidugu, who led the department's IT modernization efforts, will step down in September as turnover among federal technology leaders continues.

title: HUD's tech chief appears headed for Interior
summary: The expected pick would replace the agency's recently departed technology chief and continue a string of leadership changes.

title: No more paper: Navigating OPM’s new digital retirement process
summary: As the Office of Personnel Management completes its transition away from paper, federal employees and retirees must adapt to a streamlined — but strictly digital — process for securing their benefits.

title: Judges block Trump effort to narrow public service loan forgiveness
summary: The rulings preserve existing eligibility rules for now while testing how much authority the Education Department has to reshape a popular benefit for public service workers.

title: Unions sue to restore DOD collective bargaining rights, asserting ‘chaos’
summary: A new lawsuit alleges that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s order last April to terminate most union contracts led to a slapdash implementation process that stripped bargaining rights even from those exempt from President Trump’s anti-labor executive orders.

title: Iran War supplemental deepens FY27 budget uncertainty
summary: Congress has a lot to sort out.

title: GSA taps White House design team to revamp Login.gov
summary: The collaboration is aimed at making the government's identity platform easier to use while leaving decisions about what changes get implemented to GSA.

title: DOD's CIO says it's time to rethink the Pentagon's technology playbook
summary: Kirsten Davies said her office is shifting away from its traditional role as a backend policy shop to become a forward-leaning strategic unit.

title: Some disabled veterans say losing telework accommodations is making it harder for them to keep working at the VA
summary: Employees with disabilities at several agencies have alleged that they’re being forced to return to the office, even though the Trump administration’s directive ending telework flexibility for the civil service exempted those with qualifying reasonable accommodations.

title: Unions sue to block USDA reorganization, arguing it’s a RIF in disguise
summary: A court filing says that impacted employees must report to their new assigned locations across the country by this fall.

title: House Homeland committee seeks briefing on DHS network hack
summary: Cyber intruders accessed the unclassified network being used to help support World Cup games around the U.S., a senator said last week.

title: Trump wants to scrap a key framework for federal employee discipline
summary: Officials said the Douglas factors, 12 criteria federal agencies have used for 45 years to devise and justify discipline for misconduct, are too restrictive and “mechanistic.” Practitioners disagree.

title: Greg Barbaccia to leave federal CIO role at end of August
summary: “Greg has done an excellent job as Federal CIO and Chief AI Officer,” an OMB spokesperson told Nextgov/FCW. “He will certainly be missed when his time here comes to an end.”

title: OPM proposes ‘decentralized’ FEVS with fewer questions and less transparency
summary: Agencies would be expected to conduct their own workforce surveys each year, with little rules on how much, or how little, they divulge to the public about it.

title: Trump says Pulte can declassify ‘whatever’ he wants, sparking fears of exposing intelligence secrets
summary: “If he doesn’t care about blowing up cyber exploits, putting foreign relationships at risk, or getting people killed, he could declassify a lot,” one former official said.

title: Hackers breached DHS information-sharing network, people familiar say
summary: The Homeland Security Information Network is used by government, international and private sector partners to share sensitive but unclassified information.

title: CIA will take ‘smart risks’ and ‘course correct’ as it adopts AI, director says
summary: “We simply can’t afford to wait for a risk-free approach to emerging tech. It doesn’t exist. We have to move fast. We have to be aggressive,” CIA Director John Ratcliffe said.

title: OPM finalizes ‘Nixonian’ rule centralizing and enabling some federal firings
summary: Under final regulations published this week, the federal government’s dedicated HR agency can remove federal employees from across government over suitability and conduct issues—blocking most avenues for appeal.

title: Union accuses Treasury and HHS of neglecting telework requests from employees with disabilities
summary: The lawsuit highlights federal employees who have been waiting for more than a year to hear back about their reasonable accommodation requests as well as individuals whose need to telework ended before the agency responded.

title: Some TSP funds faltered in June
summary: Following two straight months of gains, the federal government’s 401(k)-style retirement savings program posted a more muted performance last month.
